column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names a house of fortresses and a purpose of saving me; BSB has stronghold of my deliverance.
The Hebrew describes leading and guiding with uncompleted verbs; BSB uses commands.
The Hebrew makes the trappers an active plural subject; BSB describes a net laid out for me.
The Hebrew has hand in the singular; BSB has hands.
The Hebrew names vanities of emptiness without explicitly saying idols and uses completed verbs for hating and trusting.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names the enemy’s hand; BSB says delivered me to the enemy.
The Hebrew has eye in the singular and belly; BSB has eyes and body.
The Hebrew makes my strength the subject of stumbling through my iniquity; BSB makes iniquity the subject draining strength.

The Hebrew explicitly names my soul; BSB says my life.
The Hebrew has completed verbs of trusting and saying; BSB uses present verbs.
The Hebrew has Your hand in the singular and explicitly names the enemies’ hand; BSB uses Your hands and omits their hand.
